decode_diagnosis:
Most of the gap is a measurement artefact. The rest comes from the host waiting on the GPU every step and, at long context only, from a latency floor in the attention kernel.

(1) Artefact. r1b_l_pilot.l0_a times the whole E.decode call. Its step 0 is the prefill of 32 x 512 / 1,100 tokens, and the total is divided by steps+1 = 33. The prefill alone takes 2.4-3.0 s (512) and 5.3-6.4 s (1,100) at the measured 16-19.5 TFLOP/s. The implied decode step is therefore 33-51 ms (512) and 33-70 ms (1,100), not 122-233 ms. The clean batch-32 number is L0_b's duet: 2.13 s per 32 x 40 call = about 0.27 s prefill + 46.5 ms per step, i.e. 1.3-1.9x the planned 25-35 ms. K's rollouts at 160 / 320 rows match the plan's hooked rate.

(2) Host serialisation in r1b_l_engine.decode: at least 5 GPU-to-CPU syncs per step.
- transformers 5.22.2 masking_utils._ignore_causal_mask_sdpa evaluates fast_all(padding_mask) as a Python bool (sum == numel) on every forward that receives a 2-D attention_mask, and E.decode always passes full_am. This happens before any block is launched.
- Then .cpu() of e, peos, s (plus a, a2 with the probe), nxt.tolist() for stop detection, and bool(alive.any()).
- So step time is roughly CPU (about 30-35 ms: 28 eager Qwen3 blocks plus 192 Gumbel launches) plus GPU (about 12-17 ms at B=32, short context), instead of max(CPU, GPU).
- HF generate (R's path) has the same mask sync plus a stopping-criteria sync. LCE.decode (D) has none.

(3) Per-row Gumbel: 6 launches per row per step, about 1-2 ms of CPU at 32 rows. In K's keyed rollouts the noise is drawn for all 2N rows and then sliced [:N]: about 2,000 launches per step at 320 rows. The pilot's rollout was unkeyed, so this cost was not measured.

(4) GQA: use_gqa_in_sdpa passes enable_gqa only when there is no mask. Padded batches get repeat_kv (a copy of K and V to 16 heads, every layer, every step) plus a materialised mask. This costs a few ms below 1.1K tokens and matters only at long context.

(5) Cache copies: DynamicLayer.update rewrites the whole cache with torch.cat every step. The P0-D fit gives 0.486 us per context token per row, close to the plan's 3x KV bytes. Example: 47 ms of the 171 ms step at B=3, 32K.

(6) SDPA kernel at q_len 1 in fp32: the memory-efficient kernel (3xTF32 FastF32) runs one CTA per (row, head, 64-query block), i.e. only 16 CTAs per row on 108 SMs, and each CTA walks the whole cache. The cost is 3.45 us per context token per step and does not depend on B up to about 6 rows (16K: B1 77, B2 87, B3 93 ms; 32K: B1 140, B2 155 ms). That is 8x the plan's KV-bandwidth term (0.44 us). It dominates D's long decode (D2, D3, D4) but not L's short contexts.

(7) Hooks (+3-12 %, diluted by the prefill) and Python loops are minor.

Fixes that keep the numerics (fp32, TF32 off, same kernels and values, identical tokens):
(a) E.decode without per-step syncs: keep e/peos/s/a/a2 on the GPU and copy once at the end; detect stops with torch.isin on the GPU; check alive.any() every 8 steps (extra steps after all rows have stopped are discarded and only advance the stopped rows' generators); pass the 4-D boolean padding mask that transformers would build itself (a 4-D mask skips fast_all), or None for unpadded batches. Step time becomes about max(CPU, GPU). Expected 1.2-1.4x (46 to about 35 ms).
(b) D: release the retained cache so the planned B_long=3 fits at 31.8K (about 35 % more throughput than B=2). Add an in-place preallocated KV buffer (slice-assign the new K/V, attend over a view of the filled length): same values, same kernel, same key-tile order. It removes the torch.cat rewrite: 1.1x at B=1, about 1.35x at B=3 at 28-32K. D tier 1 drops from 16.2 to 12.4 h before trims.
(c) K: draw the Gumbel noise only for the N rows that are kept. Every row has its own generator, so the kept noise is unchanged.
Each of (a)-(c) needs a bit-identity test before the freeze (logits and tokens over 32 steps at 4K and 32K), because a strided view or a changed mask path could alter dispatch.

There is no numerics-preserving fix for the q_len-1 latency floor. Split-KV (flash-decoding) or a math / cuBLAS path changes the summation order; bf16 and TF32 are excluded by the plan; CUDA graphs require StaticCache (token-identical in P0-D but not shown bit-identical) and graph-safe per-row generators. A 1-minute torch.profiler trace in P0b should confirm the kernel name and its share of the step.

code_or_config_needed: r1b_run_session.py gate_SG1 reads freeze_commit, freeze_time, plan_files and package_files, and compares against the constants FROZEN_PLAN_SHA256 / FREEZE_RECORD_SHA256 (both empty now). It does read the record, but the record cannot contain the hash of the commit that adds it. Order: freeze commit = the five plan files + package files; then the record with that freeze_commit plus the two constants in the next commit, so the ancestor check passes.

Package files: every part reads them from results/ju_space/plans/runde1b/ (C.PLAN_DIR; only r1b_d_stim also honours R1B_PKG_DIR), but they are staged in packages/. Copy all 15 (including k1_label_bank/) before the freeze and build the 3 missing ones: pilot_material.json, r1b_keys.json, l_cal.json (L-CAL, about 120 CPU-min). The same mismatch caused L0_b's 64-token fallback.
gate_SG7 only checks that pilot, trims, projection_h and funded exist. No code reads the content of pilot or projection_h (it is only recorded in manifests and provenance).
funded {tier2, items} is read by r1b_run_session.funded, Ctx.funded and r1b_report._funded. items: [] means every tier-2 item and session is funded.

trims[part] is read by Ctx.trimmed and the runner's drop_if. R needs ['RL1','RL2'] for RL2, because r1b_r_s3.py tests only 'RL1' for the dose cut at 18 / 6. D's T1-T8 and L's T2-T5 are implemented (L's trim 1 works through funded.items). K: only 'K-drop1' (K7b) and 'K-drop6' (K10a delta2) exist in code. K-drop2..5 (K9 c4/c5, K8b 16 templates, K6c(ii), K6e descriptive arms) are not implemented, so K's drop order cannot be executed beyond items 1 and 6.

D batch limits: B_long=3 and B_mid=7 are constants in r1b_d_stim.cfg, and no code reads a batch limit from the record, so 'B <= 2 at 28K/32K' could not be imposed through it. It is also unnecessary, because the P0-D OOM was the pilot's retained cache. The same bug is in the session code, though: r1b_d_d2.gen_stream (lines 102, 111) keeps the previous batch's cache alive through 'y, *_ = env.eng.decode(...)' + 'del cache'. At B_long=3 and 31.8K the second batch then needs about 51 GB (OOM on 40 GB). d2_glce3 (168-170) holds 22 GB during a 31.7K B=1 prefill (about 40 GB). The same pattern is in r1b_d_d1.p0_d (560/571/575) and r1b_d_d3.glce4 (218). Fix without any numerics change: take decode(...)[0] or del the returned cache. Only if B=3 still fails in P0b: make B_long a freeze key (engine.D.B_long), which changes cuBLAS shapes and is therefore a plan change.

models: model_pins(name, freeze) feeds ensure_model and the notebook's fetch-models (reads models[name] repo/revision/sha256). But r1b_k_s3._load35 calls ensure_model(M35, root, None), and load_model does not pass the record to registered loaders. The Qwen3.5-2B pins are therefore ignored and r1b_K_S3 / r1b_K_S7 would stop with 'revision or sha256 not pinned'. Fix: pass the freeze record to the loader.

datasets: fetch_dataset reads datasets[name] {repo, revision, allow_patterns, sha256}, which works for wikitext103 and triviaqa_rc_nocontext. 'pg19' (read by r1b_l_base.longdocs) is a GCS source (MANIFEST key 'pg19_test'), and fetch_dataset can only do Hugging Face snapshots: it needs a GCS branch with sha256 checks, or the 28 slices must ship as package files. datasets.wikitext103.k_train_offset_lines (19613) is read by r1b_k_labels. rk1_train_offset_lines is read with int() in r1b_k_rk; its default 0 would overlap D's streams, so it needs a real value once SO-PILOT is built (the draft proposes 40000).
d_streams_sha256 is read at the top level (r1b_d_stim.py:603), while main 9.1 puts it under datasets.wikitext103. Keep the top-level key; the draft carries both.

jlens: the notebook reads jlens.url (Qwen3-1.7B; the sha256 is hard-coded in r1b_core.JLENS and in the notebook and equals the HF LFS sha256 6fcc7901...) and jlens['qwen3.5-2b'] {name, sha256}. r1b_k_s3.jlens35 reads jlens['qwen3.5-2b']. All of this reads correctly. However, the notebook only copies the 2B lens from dsse_runs/r1b_inputs and never downloads it: upload it, or add a download from jlens['qwen3.5-2b'].url (sha256 69e02a97...).
decisions['OD-M14'] is read by r1b_l_b._l2a_grid ('grid_2^14' restricts L2a; any other value means the full grid). It stays undecided until P0b, because the pilot's L2a parity is invalid.

Pilot code for P0b: r1b_sessions_R.py has no r1b_P0 step (P0-R). k0_pilot lacks items 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, synchronised and warmed-up hook timing, and FISTA timing without _lip. l0_a must time decode without the prefill, on padded rows. l0_b must call probe.begin(), use real PG19 slices, time re-prefill at ~420-token histories, and measure Drive on the Drive path. p0_d must release '_' and offload base. OD-M14 needs crop / copy / L2a against a full pass at 16,384 and 32,768.

Optional speed fixes that keep the numerics, each needing a bit-identity test before the freeze: E.decode without per-step syncs, with a prebuilt 4-D padding mask; an in-place KV buffer in r1b_lce; K rollout Gumbel only for the N kept rows.
Main 9.1's table names the part files runde1b_part_R.md etc.; the actual files are runde1b_plan_teil_R/D/K/L.md. plan_files must list the real paths.

summary_de:
Der Pilot r1b_P0 reicht für das Einfrieren noch nicht. Brauchbar sind die D-Messungen (Prefill, 700-Token-Chunks, Decode B=1–3 bei 4K–32K), die K-Rollouts, die L-Leserate und die Duet-Cache-Parität.
Ungültig oder fehlend: Der R-Pilot fehlt ganz (r1b_sessions_R.py hat keinen P0-Schritt), und Qwen3.5-2B wurde nie geladen. L0 (i) teilt Prefill plus 32 Decode-Schritte durch 33, ist also keine Decode-Rate. L0 (iii) und (vii) liefen auf 64-Token-Ersatztexten, weil longdoc_slices.json nur in packages/ liegt. Der Drive-Durchsatz misst die lokale Platte. Der K-Hook-Faktor 1,89 ist ohne Synchronisation gemessen, und die 35 ms für FISTA enthalten die Lipschitz-Potenzmethode (eher 5 ms).
Der Speicherüberlauf bei B=3 (28K/32K) ist ein Artefakt: `y, *_ = …decode()` hält den vorigen Cache fest. Dasselbe Muster steckt in r1b_d_d2 (gen_stream, glce3) und würde D2 bei B=3 im echten Lauf sprengen. Das muss vor dem Einfrieren behoben werden. Eine Grenze B ≤ 2 ist nicht nötig und würde vom Code auch nicht gelesen.
Decode bei Batch 32 liegt real bei etwa 46 ms pro Schritt (Duet), nicht bei 122–233 ms. Ursachen: Host-Synchronisation in jedem Schritt (u. a. fast_all in der Maskenprüfung von transformers), das Neuschreiben des Caches per torch.cat und bei Langkontext die Latenz des fp32-Kernels bei q_len 1 (3,45 µs je Kontext-Token und Schritt, unabhängig von B).
